title: The Spear Hero and the Council of Heroes [Part 1]
text: In the end, the party swap scheduled for the next day was called off. It all started when Ren and Itsuki both refused to participate. Since my Father and I are already teaming up, if we went through with it, the story would just end with my Father and me being the strongest. After all, my party—starting with Yuki-chan—and my Father’s party are both stronger than Ren and Itsuki’s.

To be honest, there’s no point in Yuki-chan and the others leveling up on Cal Mira Island unless they’re focused on specific abilities. It’s definitely in a completely different league from the leveling we did in the first world. Even so, Father seems intent on boosting Keel and the others’ stats.

Anyway, I heard Ren finally showed up around midday the day after he got beaten to a pulp by his Assistant. The party swap was canceled, after all. He left a note in Japanese saying he was heading out hunting with his companions—almost without permission—and then vanished. And here I am, not even training Filolial-sama and the others because I heard the party swap might resume!

It seems Itsuki and the others went hunting too, not to be outdone. Well, they seem to be under the impression that their levels are already high enough. Since I and Yuki-chan raised Itsuki and his friends, a place like Cal Mira Island should be a breeze for them.

After that, it was decided that a meeting of the heroes would be held tonight, organized by Father. Trying to peek at people in the hot springs and getting scolded by Father was just part of the fun. Ren and the others didn’t show up this time.
“Well, I’m off then.”
Yuki-chan, the others, and I prepared for the meeting in the same room as my Father and the others.
“I’m supposed to go, too.”
“Huh? Melty-chan’s coming?”
My Finacée raised her hand. I wonder why? Is there a reason for my Finacée to attend a meeting on the island?
“Yes, my mother ordered me to oversee the heroes’ meeting as a representative of Melromarc.”
“I see…”
“What about Sakura and the others?”
“Since it’s a meeting of the Heroes, our companions aren’t allowed to attend. They said it might cause unnecessary commotion.”
Sakura-chan, Keel, Yuki-chan, and the others all looked displeased. On the other hand, my Assistant seemed relieved and let out a sigh of relief.
“I’m sorry, Sakura-chan.”
“No, it’s okay. But will Naofumi and the others be okay without me?”
“Well, since it’s Ren and Itsuki, I don’t think there’ll be any problems… for now. We’re just going to have a discussion.”
“Really? If anything comes up, call me anytime, okay?”
“I know, Sakura-chan.”
“Well then, we’re off.”

It was quite a struggle for me to calm Yuki-chan down, too. I can’t say I don’t understand her worries. But this is a path we simply can’t avoid if we’re going to save the world together with my Father. We have to teach Ren and Itsuki some important things as heroes.

And so, my Finacée and I headed to the meeting. For the time being, a pig that looks like a shadow is serving as our guide. We climbed the stairs leading to the stone tower and were led into a room with that round table—the one where we’d discussed the enhancement methods. Ren and Itsuki were already waiting for us.
“…Hmph.”

Both of them looked thoroughly displeased. Their gazes were even sharper than when we held the meeting in the first world. My Finacée stood at the back of the room, taking in Ren, Itsuki, and my Father and me as we took our seats.

“Now then, let us begin the information exchange among the Four Holy Heroes. I, Melty Merlomarc, Second Princess of Melromarc, will serve as the chairperson and moderator. Thank you for your cooperation.”
Then, my finacée lets her gaze wander as if trying to recall something.
“Um… This meeting was arranged as a forum for the Heroes to discuss ways to grow stronger and improve their coordination. Please bear with us.”
She sounds rather stammering. She is, after all, a childish finacée. It can’t be helped.
“Okay, let’s get this discussion started. I think there are quite a few things we need to talk about.”
“That’s right.”
“We’ll see about that…”
“Hmph.”
It seems Itsuki and Ren harbor some hostility toward us. To ignore their own ignorance like that—they’re complete clowns.

“First, Heroes, please discuss your respective teammates… Since the Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes are always working together, they’re considered to be on the same level in terms of strength, which is why we’ve arranged it this way. If you still don’t quite understand, we can resume this tomorrow.”

There’s still Yuki-chan’s group with Ren, and Keel’s group with Itsuki. Well, I feel like I’ve seen Keel’s group and Itsuki before—back when Itsuki was being held captive. At that point, Ren glared at his Father with obvious displeasure and spoke up.
“Naofumi, you’d better teach your companions some manners! I thought I was going to get killed!”
“Ah, I’d heard rumors, but as expected of Naofumi-san’s companions. It seems they lack proper training.”
In response to Ren’s words, Itsuki chimed in to back him up. What a sneaky guy.
“Are you talking about Wyndia? I’ll apologize for that, but I won’t let you say Ren isn’t at fault either.”
“What did you say? What do you think is wrong with me?!”
“From what I’ve heard from Keel, Sakura, and Wyndia, Ren, I think you might have some serious misconceptions about teamwork.”

I think so too. In Ren’s case, he seems to think everyone is just a pawn that has to follow his orders. Well, judging by your Father in the first world, that isn’t necessarily a mistake. But doesn’t that kind of thing only make sense with a large-scale unit? I think that’s the kind of command structure where you only see results when you have a force the size of an army—say, a hundred people.
“What are you talking about? It’s their fault for taking reckless actions, trying to tough it out when they should’ve dodged, and getting in the way of my attacks!”

“As a result, their coordination was a mess and they struggled in battle… or so I heard. Ren, were you perhaps under the delusion that you were the best fighter? Did you think my teammates were weak, just pawns meant to distract the enemy at best?”
“That’s not true. It’s because they didn’t follow my orders.”
I’ve heard that Keel and the others followed their orders. It just seems to me that Ren interfered after they’d already received those orders.

“He was right where they were trying to dodge an enemy attack, and he got in the way just as they were about to take the hit. He unleashed Skills just as they closed in to attack, nearly catching them in the crossfire. Just as they were about to engage in close combat, they nearly collided with the Magic support coming from the rear. I think this is a classic case of poor coordination—and that Ren himself is the one hindering their teamwork.　Or was the enemy really strong enough to warrant such a close-quarters battle?”

Father’s assessment is spot on. Given the circumstances, it’s certain that Ren was the biggest obstacle. In fact, a boss on the level of the one on Cal Mira Island is a foe that Keel and his team could defeat on their own. After all, they’ve already done it.
To begin with, if there’s a Hero present, it’s an enemy they can defeat with ease. I could take it down with a single blow.
“As proof of that, I heard the battle was already over by the time Wyndia-chan shoved Ren aside, got back up, and rushed over, right?”
“That’s not true. It was sabotage out of jealousy over Ren’s heroic performance, wasn’t it?”
Itsuki seized the opportunity to start taking Ren’s side. He probably sees us as the enemy and thinks that anything we point out must be wrong.
“Isn’t it common sense for allies to fight in a way that makes it easier for the Hero? Yet for allies to rush in and attack first… What kind of joke is that? I can’t even laugh at this.”
“Hahaha, Itsuki and Ren are idiots.”
“What did you say?”
“I’ve got nothing to do with it. That’s something Itsuki said on his own.”
Itsuki let out a strange sound at Ren’s reply. Does he think this is some kind of unexpected betrayal from Ren? Still, I’ll have my say too.
“My Father is the Shield Hero. If you think his companions would act the same way you two do, you’re not thinking things through.”
“Ugh…”

“Don’t provoke Motoyasu. Itsuki, if you don’t really understand, could you step back for a moment? You were playing a console game, weren’t you?　This is a different world, you know? It’s a problem if you keep treating it like a single-player game.”

Itsuki furrowed his brow in annoyance at Father’s words. Come to think of it, Itsuki was playing a single-player game. Maybe he’s mistaking everyone in this world—including us—for NPCs or something. No… I feel like I said back in the first world that it probably doesn’t go that far.
“If you don’t realize your opponents are human too, it’s only natural you’ll get hurt. If you’re unlucky, it might not have ended with just an injury.”
“Human? Your companions aren’t humans—they’re Demi-Humans and monsters, aren’t they?”

“…Itsuki, that’s what people call ‘nitpicking.’ Either way, they’re beings with intelligence—they can see, hear, and think for themselves—just like us. They’re no different from humans. Are you… being racist? If so, then Japan in that other world must be a very barbaric place.”
At Father’s question, Itsuki made a face as if he’d swallowed a bitter pill. Justice equating to discrimination—what a laugh. I suppose Itsuki understands that much, too.
“Kuh…”
He fell silent. But this time, Ren replied with a look of displeasure.

“Hmph. That’s what happens when you guys underestimate a fight. You do whatever you want without coordinating with my breathing. What are you going to do if you act selfishly without considering your opponent and end up in an unforeseen situation?”

Upon hearing those words, Itsuki looked as if he’d been betrayed. I don’t think Ren is on your side, though. As things stand, from Ren’s perspective—whose relationship with us has soured—we might as well be enemies. But, as they say, the enemy of my enemy isn’t necessarily my friend.

“What do you mean, ‘what are you going to do’… Ren, you’re the one who got into trouble because of that unexpected situation, aren’t you… Well, I guess I’m partly to blame for putting you in that spot, though.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not in any trouble at all. It’s that brat’s fault for not listening to me! That’s right—it’s all that brat’s fault!”
What on earth are you talking about? By “that brat,” you must mean the Assistant.
“Think about it. Partner swapping isn’t a chance to brag to the other side’s allies about how strong you are, is it?”
Ren and Itsuki quickly look away. Is that so…? I was totally under the impression this was a chance to brag about how strong we are.

“Sure, there’s that aspect to it, and I won’t deny it, but it’s also a chance to observe how strong the other side’s party members are and how they fight, right? It’s so we can learn how other heroes fight and deepen our mutual understanding, isn’t it?”
“Just watch how I fight. If you do, you’ll see that it’s the most correct way to fight in this world.”
…That’s quite a line. I consider myself pretty confident, but to boast like that is actually pretty impressive. Actually, I do understand the issues with my own fighting style as well.

By the way, the downside of my fighting style is that I rely too much on Lv. With Yuki-chan and the others, as well as my Father, we’ve gotten to the point where we’ve raised our party members’ Lv to extreme levels and then fight opponents who are far weaker than us.

I don’t think this is necessarily a bad thing myself, but compared to my Father and party members from the first world, I feel like we lack resilience. I guess you could say that even though we have the levels, we lack experience?

The thing is, since the loop began, my allies and I have never found ourselves in a critical situation. Basically, I just power through and take care of everything. In other words, we haven’t had any experience fighting opponents who are as strong as us—or stronger than us. So, there’s a possibility that we can only really hold our own against weak opponents. That’s something we’ll need to work on going forward.

Of course, my Father has picked up on that. I think that’s amazing. He was mentally prepared for the possibility of encountering a powerful enemy in any loop. This concern probably stems from the fact that “I lost in the future.” I need to be careful not to get too cocky, too.
As I was thinking about all this, the conversation between my Father and the others was moving along.
“What’s with that face? If you’re unhappy, just say so.”

“Well, then, let me tell you this. From what I’ve heard from your teammates about your behavior, it just looks to me like you’re a solo player looking down on others, brainwashing and training your juniors just like Itsuki does.”
“What did you say! You’re saying I’m the same as Itsuki!? Don’t mess with me!”
Ren slammed his hands on the table as he stood up abruptly and glared at my Father. So, he’s furious when confronted with the facts?
